headline: LPG price jumps Tk 223 in a month; official retail price exceeds Tk 2,000
summary: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has increased the official price of a 12kg LPG cylinder to Tk 2,060 for November, marking the first time it has crossed the Tk 2,000 mark.
details: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has increased the official retail price of a 12kg LPG cylinder by Tk 223 to Tk 2,060 for November. This is the first time the official price has exceeded Tk 2,000.

The official price has risen by Tk 475, or nearly 30 percent, over the last two months. This comes after LPG traders threatened a nationwide shutdown of sales and distribution to demand higher commissions.

Under the new structure, charges for storage, bottling, and distribution have all increased. Storage and bottling charges rose by 40 percent, while distributors' charges jumped 70 percent and retailers' charges rose by 55 percent.
The new price is higher than the Tk 1,976 proposed by BERC's technical evaluation committee. The increase is based on the international Saudi Aramco contract price, which has risen to $759 per tonne.
Consumer representatives from the Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB) have questioned the rationale for the increase, as consumers were already paying between Tk 2,000 and Tk 2,200 since March.
CAB officials have demanded an investigation into allegations of artificial shortages, hoarding, and overcharging before any further price adjustments were made.
caption:
LPG prices just hit a record high. A 12kg cylinder now officially costs Tk 2,060.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has increased the official retail price of a 12kg LPG cylinder by Tk 223 to Tk 2,060 for November. This is the first time the official price has exceeded Tk 2,000.

The official price has risen by Tk 475, or nearly 30 percent, over the last two months. This comes after LPG traders threatened a nationwide shutdown of sales and distribution to demand higher commissions.

Under the new structure, charges for storage, bottling, and distribution have all increased. Storage and bottling charges rose by 40 percent, while distributors' charges jumped 70 percent and retailers' charges rose by 55 percent.

The new price is higher than the Tk 1,976 proposed by BERC's technical evaluation committee. The increase is based on the international Saudi Aramco contract price, which has risen to $759 per tonne.

Consumer representatives from the Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB) have questioned the rationale for the increase, as consumers were already paying between Tk 2,000 and Tk 2,200 since March.

CAB officials have demanded an investigation into allegations of artificial shortages, hoarding, and overcharging before any further price adjustments were made.

headline: Shakib, Litton in Diamond tier as Tigers flock to APL draft
summary: A large contingent of Bangladeshi cricketers, including stars like Shakib Al Hasan and Litton Das, have registered for the Afghanistan Premier League draft.
details: Bangladesh stars Shakib Al Hasan and Litton Das are among many Bangladeshi cricketers who have registered for the upcoming Afghanistan Premier League (APL) draft.

The draft, scheduled for November 3 in Dubai, will see the players placed in different categories. Shakib and Litton, along with Tawhid Hridoy, Shoriful Islam, and Nahid Rana, are in the premier Diamond category.
Seasoned players like Mushfiqur Rahim, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, and Rishad Hossain have been placed in the Platinum tier.
The Gold category includes a dozen more Tigers, including Mahmudullah, Afif Hossain, and Hasan Mahmud.
In total, 462 players will be auctioned across five tiers, including Silver and Emerging categories, featuring international stars like Wanindu Hasaranga and Fakhar Zaman.
The revamped five-team APL is expected to start on December 27, likely in the UAE rather than Afghanistan.
The league was previously launched in 2018 but was scrapped after one season due to payment disputes and integrity concerns.
caption:
Shakib, Litton and a huge contingent of Bangladesh stars are heading to the APL draft!

Bangladesh stars Shakib Al Hasan and Litton Das are among many Bangladeshi cricketers who have registered for the upcoming Afghanistan Premier League (APL) draft.

The draft, scheduled for November 3 in Dubai, will see the players placed in different categories. Shakib and Litton, along with Tawhid Hridoy, Shoriful Islam, and Nahid Rana, are in the premier Diamond category.

Seasoned players like Mushfiqur Rahim, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, and Rishad Hossain have been placed in the Platinum tier.

The Gold category includes a dozen more Tigers, including Mahmudullah, Afif Hossain, and Hasan Mahmud.

In total, 462 players will be auctioned across five tiers, including Silver and Emerging categories, featuring international stars like Wanindu Hasaranga and Fakhar Zaman.

The revamped five-team APL is expected to start on December 27, likely in the UAE rather than Afghanistan.

The league was previously launched in 2018 but was scrapped after one season due to payment disputes and integrity concerns.
